commitResults.messageBody:
Duke is only the starter name and needs to be replaced for Level-0.

Rename the main class and update the documentation to use Green Chonk.
Add a short animated greeting and farewell to give the chatbot its own
personality.

Read input until the user enters bye and echo every other command
unchanged. Update the README with the new interaction.

Store up to 100 tasks in memory and display them with one-based
numbering when the user enters list. Update the README with the new
interaction.

Use Green Chonk-themed acknowledgements and list messages so each
action has a clear response. Shorten the animation delay to keep the
text interface responsive and update the README transcript.
Represent tasks as objects so each task owns its completion state. Support mark and unmark commands and show status icons in task listings.
Represent each task type as a Task subclass so completion behavior stays shared while type-specific details remain encapsulated. Parse the Level 4 command formats and document their output.

Keep expected CLI behavior in a versioned test plan and compile each run with Java 25. The harness prints every transcript and stops at the first missing output fragment so regressions are easy to diagnose.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow blank commands in UI tests
commitResults.messageBody: Permit empty input strings so the harness can exercise the chatbot's blank-command error path while continuing to reject empty output expectations. Document the distinction in the project-local skill.

Validate command syntax and task numbers before mutating the task list, and report failures through GreenChonkException so malformed input cannot terminate the session. Document the new feedback and cover valid and invalid commands together to verify state remains intact.

Store tasks in an ArrayList so delete can remove the selected item and the remaining numbering comes directly from the collection. Reuse task-number validation for invalid requests, and document and test the new command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Represent task status with an enum
commitResults.messageBody: Replace boolean completion flags with named states so mark and unmark calls make their intent clear. Keep each status icon with its corresponding enum value.

Green Chonk loses its task list when the application exits.

Persist task changes in a relative file and restore them at startup.

Create storage on first use and isolate UI tests from saved data.

Deadline and event dates are stored as unvalidated text.

Parse ISO dates into LocalDate values and display them consistently.

Reject invalid dates before they can enter the task list or data file.

Events can be created with an ending date earlier than their start.

Enforce the date-order invariant and report invalid event commands.

Treat impossible ranges in saved data as corrupted records.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show tasks scheduled on a date
commitResults.messageBody:
Task dates are only visible when listing the entire task collection.

Add a schedule query for deadlines and inclusive event ranges.

Keep original task numbers so matching tasks remain actionable.

GreenChonk mixes command orchestration with terminal input and output.

Move command reading, banners, task feedback, and errors behind Ui.

Preserve the dialogue while establishing a clear presentation boundary.

GreenChonk owns file access and storage parsing alongside commands.

Move loading, saving, serialization, and record validation into Storage.

Keep the relative path, UTF-8 format, and rollback behavior unchanged.

Application logic shares a mutable task list across UI and storage.

Introduce TaskList as the owner of task ordering and mutations.

Route display, storage, rollback, and schedules through its API.

GreenChonk mixes command interpretation with app coordination.

Move task syntax, date parsing, and index validation into Parser.

Preserve every existing validation message and command boundary.

GreenChonk previously owned command dispatch and each operation's
execution logic.

Have Parser create commands that act on the task list, UI, and storage.
This keeps the main loop focused on parsing, execution, and exit state
while retaining validation and persistence rollback behavior.

All production classes previously shared the unnamed package, which hid
the boundaries established by the object-oriented refactor.

Move each class under its responsibility-based package and update launch
targets accordingly. Keep package dependencies acyclic and preserve
command and persistence behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure Gradle to build Green Chonk
commitResults.messageBody:
The supplied Gradle branch still targets the template Duke entry point.

Point the application task at Green Chonk and document the wrapper as
the default terminal build and run workflow.

Core parsing, persistence, task, and command behavior previously relied
only on end-to-end console checks.

Add isolated tests for valid, invalid, boundary, and rollback paths.
Document the Gradle test command so future increments can check
regressions quickly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Green Chonk as an executable JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The Shadow plugin still used the starter duke.jar name, which made
the distributable inconsistent with the application identity.

Rename the fat JAR to greenchonk.jar and document how to build,
locate, and smoke-test it from an empty folder.

Several public entry points and command side effects were undocumented,
and important parsing, storage, and UI helpers required source reading
to understand their contracts.

Add Javadocs for every generated public API element and the nontrivial
private helpers. Make implicit constructors explicit so Gradle can
generate warning-free API documentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Java code with SE-EDU conventions
commitResults.messageBody:
Some Javadoc tags lack their required punctuation, the entry point and
public command constructors are undocumented, and a test collection
uses a singular name.

Apply the course naming, import, layout, and documentation rules so the
codebase follows one consistent standard. Keep runtime behavior
unchanged and make generated Javadocs warning-free.

Future Java changes need a durable project-local reference to the
course's basic and intermediate rules.

Add a focused skill covering naming, layout, statements, Javadocs, and
verification. Require agents to load it before changing Java code so
the standard remains part of every later increment.

Future commits need a durable project-local reference to the course
message and branch conventions.

Add a focused skill covering imperative subjects, rationale-driven
bodies, line limits, branch names, and pre-commit review. Require
agents to load it before proposing or creating Git metadata.

Users cannot locate tasks by description without scanning the full list.

Add case-insensitive substring matching with clear missing-keyword and
no-match feedback. Preserve each match's original list number so later
mark, unmark, and delete commands target the task that was shown.

Integrate the coding-standard work after A-JavaDoc while preserving the
API documentation added by the earlier merge.

Resolve overlapping Javadocs by retaining complete descriptions and
required punctuation, so both increments remain represented.

Integrate task keyword search with the completed documentation and
coding-standard work.

Keep the find feedback methods beside the documented task-count helper.
This preserves both search behavior and coding quality.

Style mistakes are currently caught only through manual review.

Add the SE-EDU configuration to Gradle so builds check both production
and test sources. Bring the existing tests into compliance and document
how to run the checks locally.

Introduce an FXML-based desktop interface that delegates commands to
the existing application engine. Keep the CLI available for automated
testing and package JavaFX dependencies for all supported platforms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Green Chonk mascot in chat
commitResults.messageBody:
Green Chonk's replies use a generic text-only avatar.

Display the supplied mascot artwork in bot dialogs while retaining the
compact text avatar for user messages. Package the image with the app
and clip it to the existing circular treatment.

Multi-line replies allow the avatar container to grow with the dialog
row.

Constrain both avatar dimensions and disable row-height filling so each
portrait remains a consistent circle regardless of response length.

Avatars currently sit at the top of multi-line message bubbles.

Anchor bot and user avatars to the bottom edge so each speaker remains
visually connected to the end of the corresponding message.

Java 25 warns when JavaFX loads its native windowing library.

Grant native access only to javafx.graphics for Gradle launches and
document the matching option for IntelliJ and executable JAR runs. This
keeps startup warning-free and prepares for stricter future JDKs.

Multi-line responses repeat direct println calls throughout Ui.

Centralize ordered line output in a varargs helper so callers can supply
two or three lines without constructing temporary arrays. Preserve all
existing response text and ordering.

Users need a discoverable way to learn Green Chonk's command syntax.

Add a read-only help command that lists every supported command and the
required date format. Document it and cover the behavior at command,
parser, and command-line UI levels.

Requiring ISO input makes otherwise valid calendar dates cumbersome to
enter.

Accept strict ISO, day/month/year, and English text formats through a
shared date utility while preserving ISO persistence and the existing
display format. Rename date fields and accessors to express their domain
meaning.

Storage mixes filesystem access with task serialization and data
validation, making both responsibilities harder to test and evolve.

Move the line format into a focused TaskCodec and report persistence
failures through StorageException while retaining their original causes.
Keep the existing file format fully compatible.

Writing directly to the data file can leave it incomplete if a save is
interrupted.

Write each snapshot to a sibling temporary file, then atomically
replace the data file. Fall back if atomic moves are unavailable.
Clean up failed temporary files and retain I/O causes for diagnosis.
